title: Hierarchy of topological superconductivity generated via heterostructures of unconventional $p$-wave magnets
abstract: A theoretical framework is proposed to engineer both first and second-order topological superconducting phases in a two-dimensional (2D) heterostructure, consisting of a quantum spin Hall insulator (QSHI) and an unconventional $p$-wave magnet in presence of proximity-induced $s$-wave superconducting pairing. Our analysis establishes that the transitions between the trivial and topological superconducting (TSC) phases can be regulated though the parameters of $p$-wave magnet. Presence of chiral symmetry leads to the characterization of both types of TSC phases by the respective invariants, one-dimensional winding number and quadrupolar winding number. These results are supplemented by an analytical effective low-energy edge theory that yields a deeper insight into the emergence of the different topological phases of the system. Bulk pairing analysis reveals the competition between the effective $(p_x+p_y)$ and $(p_x+ip_y)$ type pairings that are governed by the intrinsic spin-orbit coupling inherited to the QSHI and spin-split bands of the $p$-wave magnet, respectively.
summary: This theoretical study proposes a method to create and control a hierarchy of topological superconducting phases (FOTSC and SOTSC) in a heterostructure combining a QSHI and a p-wave magnet. By analyzing the BdG Hamiltonian and using topological invariants, the authors show that these distinct phases can be tuned by magnetic coupling, leading to the emergence of Majorana corner modes and unique edge states.
main_problem: The paper aims to theoretically engineer and characterize the hierarchy of topological superconducting (TSC) phases, specifically first-order (FOTSC) and second-order (SOTSC), in a novel heterostructure.
main_result: The model successfully demonstrates the tunability of both FOTSC and SOTSC phases by adjusting the magnetic coupling parameter, leading to distinct topological signatures like Majorana corner modes (MCMs) and different edge mode behaviors.
method: The analysis employs the Bogoliubov-de Gennes (BdG) Hamiltonian, utilizing symmetry invariants (winding numbers) and deriving low-energy edge theories to classify the topological phases.
model_or_system: The physical system is a 2D heterostructure composed of a Quantum Spin Hall Insulator (QSHI), an unconventional p-wave magnet (pWM), and proximity-induced s-wave superconductivity. The system is modeled using the BdG Hamiltonian, which incorporates contributions from the QSHI and pWM.
key_observables: Topological phases (Trivial, FOTSC, SOTSC), 1D winding number, quadrupolar winding number, Majorana corner modes (MCMs), and Majorana flat/dispersive edge modes.
important_parameters: The coupling parameter $J_{sd}$ (from the pWM) and the superconducting gap $\Delta_0$ are key tunability parameters.
main_assumptions: The analysis relies on deriving effective low-energy Hamiltonians by approximating trigonometric functions near the $\Gamma$ point and applying boundary conditions (OBC) for edge/corner mode analysis.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the eigenvalue spectra showing transitions between phases based on $J_{sd}$, and depict the localized MCMs in the SOTSC phase.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by establishing the full BdG model, deriving effective low-energy edge and bulk Hamiltonians, characterizing the topological invariants (winding numbers), and finally mapping out the phase diagram showing the emergence of FOTSC and SOTSC regimes.
why_interesting: This work provides a detailed theoretical roadmap for realizing and controlling multiple distinct topological superconducting states using engineered material heterostructures, which is highly relevant for topological quantum computation.
